title: Recording: Rudolph The Red-Nosed Reggae by Paul McCartney | 1975
content:
Studio Three, EMI Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Richard Lush

Paul McCartney recorded the ‘Wonderful Christmastime’ b-side ‘Rudolph The Red-Nosed Reggae’ on 12 May 1975.

He had booked EMI Studios to record music for the soundtrack of a David Litchfield film about karate, which was being produced by MPL. With Wings on a temporary hiatus after completing Venus And Mars, he decided to record a series of solo pieces.

McCartney arranged the hire of a number of instruments for the session, including harpsichord, a drum kit, and Japanese percussion instruments, from London company Maurice Placquet. The delivery drivers included Bob Loveday, who was a violinist. McCartney invited him to take part in the session, for which he was paid a standard fee of £25.

The first piece was titled ‘Sea Dance’. It had McCartney playing a grand piano, and Loveday multitracking violin parts to give the impression of many instruments.

He had this notion for a big string orchestra sweeping theme tune, and he got me to record track after track of violins – I think it was about eight in all when he’d finished. It sounded absolutely mighty when it was done.
Bob Loveday, 8 July 2024
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 2: 1974-80

The other pieces for the Litchfield film were ‘Karate Chaos’, ‘Piano, Violin, Etc.’, and ‘Backwards One’, in which McCartney and Loveday were joined by Linda McCartney.

Towards the end of the session, which saw copious amounts of cannabis smoked by the musicians, Paul decided to record an unseasonal reggae version of ‘Rudolph The Red-Nosed Reindeer’ featuring him on harpsichord and Loveday on violin. McCartney then overdubbed piano, bass guitar, and drums.

We worked all night, and at 8am they wandered off and I was left in the studio completely stoned out of my mind on popstar grade cannabis!
Bob Loveday, 8 July 2024
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 2: 1974-80

‘Rudolph The Red-Nosed Reggae’ was released on the ‘Wonderful Christmastime’ single in November 1979. It was the first single credited solely to McCartney since ‘Another Day’ in 1971.
